record.summary: Requires frontier developers (of foundation models trained with over 10^26 operations) to publish a transparency report before deploying a new or substantially modified model, and large frontier developers (revenue above USD 500 million) to publish and follow a frontier AI framework for managing catastrophic risks, publish risk-assessment summaries and file disclosure statements. Critical safety incidents must be reported within 72 hours, or within 24 hours to an appropriate authority if death or serious injury is imminent. An office in the Department of Financial Services oversees compliance; the Attorney General can seek penalties of up to USD 1 million, or 3 million for later violations.
record.notes: Both houses passed S6953-B (same as A6453-B) on 12 Jun 2025; it was delivered to the Governor on 9 Dec 2025 and signed on 19 Dec 2025 as Chapter 699 of 2025, with approval memo 76, the Governor announcing agreed chapter amendments. The chapter amendment S8828 (same as A9449) passed the Senate on 28 Jan 2026 and the Assembly on 11 Mar 2026 and was signed on 27 Mar 2026 as Chapter 96 of 2026. It repealed and replaced Article 44-B of the General Business Law as first enacted: a revenue test of over USD 500 million replaced the test of over USD 100 million in compute costs, the ban on deploying a frontier model that would create an unreasonable risk of critical harm was dropped, maximum penalties fell from USD 10 million and 30 million to 1 million and 3 million, and the effective date moved from the ninetieth day after enactment to 1 Jan 2027. Large frontier developers must also send the office summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use every three months and pay assessments to fund it. The office's annual reports begin on 1 Jan 2028. Accredited colleges and universities doing academic research and the Empire AI consortium are exempt, and there is no private right of action. The Governor described the law as building on California's recently adopted framework.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: nysenate.gov refused the archiver (HTTP 403) on 11, 16 and 17 Oct 2026, so the record now rests on the Assembly's bill pages for A6453 (same as S6953-B) and A9449 (same as S8828) and on the Governor's press release of 19 Dec 2025, stored from nyassembly.gov and governor.ny.gov on 17 Oct 2026. The A6453 page gives the actions of both houses, 'SIGNED CHAP.699' and 'APPROVAL MEMO.76' on 12/19/2025, and the text as signed. The A9449 page gives the actions, including 'SIGNED CHAP.96' on 03/27/2026, and the Assembly print of the chapter amendment with the new Article 44-B and the effective date of 1 Jan 2027; the Senate print S8828 that was signed was not stored, and the page lists the two as the same bill. The release confirms the signature, 72-hour reporting, the oversight office in the Department of Financial Services and the penalties.

judgment.status_reasoning: Chapter 96 of 2026 ('03/27/2026 SIGNED CHAP.96') amended section 3 of Chapter 699 to read 'This act shall take effect ... January 1, 2027', and section 5 makes the new Article 44-B take effect on that date. 1 Jan 2027 is after 18 Oct 2026, so 'Adopted, not yet in force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific state law on frontier AI developers' safety frameworks, incident reporting and oversight; in scope with no note (unchanged).
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 19 Dec 2025, the signature as Chapter 699 (A6453 page; the Governor's release of that date). date_last_updated 27 Mar 2026, the signature of the chapter amendment as Chapter 96. date_in_force 1 Jan 2027 from the amended section 3.

open_questions: The text of the chapter amendment comes from the Assembly print A9449; the Senate print S8828, which was signed as Chapter 96, was not stored (nysenate.gov refuses the archiver). The Assembly page lists them as the same bill; a stored copy of S8828 or of the chaptered law would confirm the wording.
